lc_person: Philip Jeremy Graham, born 1932; child psychiatrist at the Hospital for Sick Children and emeritus professor of child psychiatry at the Institute of Child Health, London.
item_person: Philip Graham, born 1951; novelist, short-story writer and editor associated with the University of Illinois; the item also contains identifiers belonging to the child psychiatrist.

evidence.says: LC names Graham, P. J. (Philip Jeremy), cites a British Library authority record giving birth year 1932, and identifies him through Epidemiological approaches in child psychiatry (1977), with a Hospital for Sick Children affiliation, and So young, so sad, so listen (1995). LC links VIAF 24769067, GND 120002256, ISNI 0000000117514065 and Q7183636.

The item describes a novelist and editor, gives birth year 1951, and links the Wikipedia article Philip Graham (writer). It also asserts occupation psychiatrist and carries LC n78016916 and the same VIAF, GND and ISNI identifiers as the psychiatrist's LC record. These assertions conflate two people.

Graham's own website identifies him as emeritus professor of child psychiatry at the Institute of Child Health, London, and a former consultant at the Hospital for Sick Children, Great Ormond Street. It lists The End of Adolescence and So Young, So Sad, So Listen among his publications.

The graph's Open Library author, P. J. Graham, includes Epidemiological approaches in child psychiatry and So young, so sad, so listen, matching LC's cited works, as well as The end of adolescence and Susan Isaacs: a life freeing the minds of children. The author page also contains unrelated-looking titles, so its whole bibliography should not be assumed to represent one person.

The University of Illinois identifies Philip Graham as a professor of English, director of its Creative Writing Program, author of two short-story collections and a novel, and fiction editor of Ninth Letter. This independently establishes the writer's distinct field and affiliation.

notes: The supported birth year is for the LC psychiatrist. This is a conflated Wikidata item, rather than a simple birth-year typo: its description, birth statement and Wikipedia sitelink identify the writer, while its authority identifiers identify the psychiatrist. The graph's LC assignment fits its name and matching Open Library works. No separate QID for the psychiatrist was confidently identified.
